process: The author is inventing real physics: a thin-film glaze solver whose result matched a museum pot without being told to, and a viscous glass sheet that matches the textbook growth rate to 0.5%. That is the radical, own-idea work goal 8 asks for, and it moves goals 3 and 7 on paper. But the player's island did not get better this session. The noon sun football (an old, excellent idea) is invisible and makes every lunchtime look broken. The chick double and Lumi's 9 Hz vibration from earlier reviews are untouched. This session's outputs are an invisible jar, a snowball film behind a slab (the same untested-camera mistake as s129, which the journal admits) and an unreadable glass film. Goals: 1 (interactions) is stalled, with the mini games unchanged and the new toys unplayable. 2 has no release candidate. 3 and 8 moved in simulation, not in the game. 4 and 6 are flat: good light after 13:30, broken around noon, animation still vibrating. 5: Lumi stands at its workbench, but is bored every session. Before the potter's wheel and glass in Jump in, spend one session on what a visitor sees in the first minute: make the sun-ball hour read (or shorten it), one Lumi that stands still, and the glass film finished and framed close. My review covered all four mini games for about a minute each through interact! (reviews/p142/play), free, follow and orbit cameras four times from 13:17 to 13:42 (reviews/p142/cam-*), and progress shots 0020, 0139, 0141 and 0142 side by side. My attempt to put Lumi beside the jar in Jump in did not take: Lumi stayed by the swing, so I could not test the jar by hand.

animation.why: live_motion: 6 of 10 move well. Lumi's beak, body and face turn back 9 times a second, and its crest swings at 6.2 m/s. Pinchy vibrates at 9 Hz, Truffle judders (44%), and Sir Sniffsalot's tail jumps 0.17 m in one frame. The jug film is clean. The snowball film has 50 jumps (fade-in and camera drift).

camera.why: At 13:17 the follow camera shows only empty sea and one tree top (p142/cam-follow-1-h13.29.png). In Jump in the follow camera sits behind a bush filling half the frame (p142/play/jumpin-2.png). The creatures sheet has a creature lost in a crown and Pinchy behind a slab. The snowball film is shot from behind a slab. At 13:33 follow and 13:42 orbit the composition is good.

creatures.why: Faces read well up close, and the 13:33 dance crowd (sheep, crab with party hat, pigs) is charming. A second, smaller yellow bird follows Lumi in every mini game and in the follow and traced views.

fun.why: I played all four games for about a minute each through interact!. Firefly catch has a clear card, 'Time's up 1/8', a tip and a lantern reward. Hide and seek gives 'a giggle 22 m to your left'. Berry race gives 'The critters win 2 to 0' with a tip. Jump in has 25+ keys of toys. All work and invite a replay, but none changed, and nothing this session is playable: the jar does nothing and the snowball is not in the game.

lighting.why: Outside the sun-ball hour the raster is bright and warm (13:41: blue sky, saturated greens, a rainbow over the sea; p142/cam-free-4-h13.69.png). From 12:00 to 13:30 the sky sits at 0.1 and the island goes olive and black-green, with no visible cause. The traced still in that hour has a low golden key and long shadows, nicer than the raster, but grainy with firefly speckle.

materials.why: The jar's glaze comes from a real thickness simulation, a strong idea, but on film it reads as matte olive plastic with raised-looking lines. The coat shows in one glint, with no depth and no pale rim. The glass film, which could show transmission and glowing glass, is unreadable. The sea is still the only convincing material.

performance.why: 30 fps, frame median 2.9 ms, p95 6.4 ms, also through four mini games. Path tracing toggles on and off without crashing (the 0139 crash is fixed).

props.why: Generated trees, mushrooms, easels, swing and lantern hold up. The new jar is invisible at 14 cm on the meadow, and I did not find it from any camera.

style.why: The cozy toy style holds up and is cohesive in good light. The noon dusk turns it into muddy olive and brown, and the yellow double makes Lumi's silhouette ambiguous.

ui.why: Mini game cards and HUDs are readable and helpful. Jump in's key card covers the bottom third of the view and its lines run off the left edge ('splashes)' is cut). 'Things to try' never mentions the jar, the chip stone or the sun football.

world.why: Same island: cottage, pond, easels, floating palm islands, pier. It reads well at 13:40 but is unreadable during the noon dusk. A black untextured box stands on the shore near the hut (p142/play/jumpin-4.png).

wow.why: The last posts: a still jar, a snowball miss, a chip-stone take 2, an ant miss, a lantern knock. Four of the last ten are misses. The glass bubble, the one with spectacle, has an unreadable mp4. The sun football hour could be the island's biggest wow and is invisible.

summary: For an island hour and a half around noon the island looks broken. sunball.jl (s122) dims the sky to 0.1 and aims a low sun from a ball on the meadow, but the ball shows in none of my views. A player sees murky dusk at midday, and every progress shot is taken in that hour. After 13:30 the island is at its best: bright, colourful, a rainbow, friends dancing with music notes. The four mini games still work and give clear feedback, but none changed. This session's new things (a 14 cm jar, a snowball film shot from behind a slab, a glass film that does not play) are original ideas that do not reach a player yet.
